md_description: This workflow covers genetically modified plant lines expressing tagged proteins of interest, preparation of plant cells for transmission electron microscopy, immunogold labeling, and TEM imaging of subcellular compartments. It captures the resulting raw micrographs and computationally derives protein localization outputs used to study photosynthetic efficiency and stress-response roles. The DAG also documents critical experimental metadata such as plant genotype and phenotype, embedding and sectioning protocols, TEM acquisition settings, and image resolution parameters.

gm_plant_line.reasoning: For the gm_plant_line Entity node, I included only intrinsic identity/origin metadata for the transgenic plant line and excluded any preparation, labeling, imaging, or computational fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating experiment-level identifiers and any fields that would overlap with downstream nodes such as embedding, section thickness, antibody details, TEM settings, file properties, or localization outputs. Given the experiment description, the key needs here are the plant species/background, the transgene/tagged protein construct, genotype status, and observable phenotype relevant to interpreting TEM localization. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no need to de-duplicate against existing names.

md_schema.descr: Plant species used for the transgenic line, recorded at the entity level before tissue preparation; use the accepted taxon name or common lab species name, e.g. Arabidopsis thaliana or Nicotiana benthamiana.
Parental/ecotype background of the plant line as maintained for the experiment, recorded once for the line identity; examples include Col-0, WS-2, or a named cultivar.

Identity of the introduced construct encoding the tagged protein of interest, including the expressed protein name and tag if applicable; record the construct designation used for the line, e.g. GFP-fusion, HA-tagged, or Myc-tagged protein name.
Genotype description of the plant line at the time the sample was sourced, including zygosity or allele status when relevant; for example, homozygous, heterozygous, or segregating line designation.

Visible or recorded phenotype of the genetically modified plant line relevant to interpreting TEM localization and stress/photosynthetic studies, captured at the entity stage before fixation; use a short free-text description such as dwarfism, chlorosis, or no obvious phenotype.
Selectable or screenable marker carried by the transgenic line, if used to maintain the line or identify transformants; examples include antibiotic resistance or fluorescent marker names.
Internal or breeder-assigned identifier for the specific transgenic plant line used in this workflow, recorded as a string example such as line_17, T2-5, or OE-3.

fix_plant_tissue.reasoning: For the fix_plant_tissue Process node, I included only process-level fixation parameters that describe how the tissue was chemically preserved prior to embedding. I excluded plant identity/phenotype fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded embedding, sectioning, labeling, capture, signal, and derivative details because those belong to later nodes. Since no already_generated fields were provided in this turn, there were no exact duplicates to avoid. The chosen fields focus on fixation chemistry, timing, temperature, and buffer conditions, plus a preservation-quality indicator that is intrinsic to the fixation step and useful for reproducibility of ultrastructure and epitope retention.

md_schema.descr: Primary chemical fixative used to preserve plant cell ultrastructure and immunogold epitopes prior to embedding; record the reagent name(s), e.g. glutaraldehyde, paraformaldehyde, or a mixed fixative.

Concentration of the primary fixative solution used during tissue fixation, measured at the fixation step before embedding; report as percent w/v or v/v as appropriate for the reagent, typically in the range 0.1-5.0.
Buffer used to prepare or dilute the fixative during the fixation step, recorded at the time tissue was immersed or infiltrated; examples include phosphate buffer or cacodylate buffer.
pH of the fixation buffer during chemical fixation, measured at the fixation step; typical range is 6.5-8.0 and should match the buffered fixation solution used for preserving plant ultrastructure.
Temperature at which the plant tissue was chemically fixed, measured during the fixation incubation; typically 4-25 degrees Celsius depending on protocol.
Total time the tissue remained in fixative, recorded for the fixation incubation prior to embedding; report in minutes, typically ranging from 10 minutes to many hours depending on tissue type.
Number of buffer or solvent rinses performed after primary fixation and before embedding, recorded as an integer count at the end of the fixation step.

Qualitative assessment of how well cellular ultrastructure was preserved after fixation, recorded immediately after the fixation step and before embedding; use standardized terms such as excellent, acceptable, or poor.

embedded_tissue.reasoning: For the embedded_tissue Entity node, I included only intrinsic properties of the resin-embedded plant tissue that result from the embedding step and are needed to understand downstream sectioning. I excluded fixation details because those belong to the upstream fixation process, and I excluded section thickness, grid placement, labeling, imaging, file, and computed outputs because those belong to downstream nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied here, so there were no explicit duplicates to avoid. The fields focus on the embedding medium, embedding protocol identity, curing conditions, and resulting block qualities that describe the entity produced by this step without crossing into sectioning or TEM territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the resin or embedding medium used to infiltrate and embed the fixed plant tissue, recorded as the entity's material composition before sectioning; examples include epoxy resin, LR White, or Spurr's resin.
Identifier or short name of the embedding protocol applied to the fixed tissue, recorded for the embedded block identity; use the lab protocol name, version, or shorthand if available.

Temperature used during resin infiltration and/or polymerization for the embedding step, recorded as the block was prepared before sectioning; typical range is 20-70 degrees Celsius depending on resin chemistry.

Total duration of the embedding procedure, including infiltration and curing as applicable, measured in hours for the block produced prior to sectioning; typical range is several hours to several days.
Qualitative hardness of the cured embedded tissue block as assessed before ultrathin sectioning; use the level that best matches sectioning behavior, e.g. soft, medium, or hard.

Orientation of the tissue within the resin block that affects later ultrathin sectioning, recorded at the entity stage after embedding; examples include transverse, longitudinal, or mixed orientation.

Whether the resin embedding step completed curing successfully for the block prior to sectioning; use this to indicate whether the embedded tissue is fully polymerized and ready for ultrathin sectioning.

section_tissue.reasoning: For the section_tissue Process node, I included only sectioning-process parameters that describe how ultrathin sections were produced from the embedded block. I excluded block composition and hardness because those belong to the upstream embedded_tissue Entity, and I excluded section dimensions as a resulting material property because those belong to the downstream ultrathin_sections Entity. I also excluded immunogold labeling and TEM capture details because they are later steps. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no duplicates to avoid. The selected fields capture the operational sectioning setup needed for reproducibility: instrument type, knife/blade, target thickness, cutting conditions, and section collection media.

md_schema.descr: Model or name of the ultramicrotome used to cut the embedded plant tissue into ultrathin sections, recorded at the sectioning step; include manufacturer and model when available, e.g. Leica UC7 or RMC PT-XL.
Type of knife or blade used during ultrathin sectioning of the embedded block, recorded during the sectioning process; examples include glass knife, diamond knife, or histo knife.
Target thickness of the ultrathin sections produced from the embedded tissue, specified at the sectioning step before collection; report in nanometers, typically in the range 40-120 nm for TEM.

Cutting speed of the ultramicrotome during section production, recorded as the blade advances through the embedded block at the sectioning step; typical range is slow and controlled, for example 0.1-2.0 mm/s.
Clearance or cutting angle used for ultrathin sectioning, recorded at the sectioning step to control section quality; report in degrees, commonly within 1-15 degrees depending on knife and resin.

Medium used to collect or float the ultrathin sections after cutting, recorded at the end of the sectioning step; examples include water bath, copper grid, or adhesive film depending on the collection workflow.
Qualitative assessment of the sectioning outcome at the end of the process, based on whether sections were intact and suitable for TEM; use standardized terms such as good, acceptable, or poor.

ultrathin_sections.reasoning: For the ultrathin_sections Entity node, I included only intrinsic properties of the produced sections that describe what the sections are and how they are physically characterized before immunogold labeling. I excluded the sectioning instrument and cutting parameters because those belong to the upstream section_tissue process, and I excluded labeling, TEM capture, raw file, and computed analysis fields because those belong to downstream nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior field names to avoid duplicating. The selected fields cover the minimum section identity and physical characteristics needed for downstream labeling and imaging: thickness, grid support, section count, and basic section integrity.

md_schema.descr: Measured thickness of the ultrathin section as collected on the grid after sectioning, recorded at the entity stage before immunogold labeling; report in nanometers, typically around 40-120 nm for TEM.
Material of the TEM support grid carrying the ultrathin section, recorded as a physical property of the section entity before labeling; examples include copper, nickel, or gold.
Mesh size of the TEM grid supporting the ultrathin section, recorded as the section is prepared for labeling and imaging; common values include 50, 75, 100, or 200 mesh.
Number of ultrathin sections mounted on a single TEM grid after sectioning, recorded before immunogold labeling; this is an integer count used to track section loading density.

Qualitative assessment of section condition after cutting and mounting, recorded before immunogold labeling; use standardized terms such as intact, wrinkled, or torn to indicate usability for downstream TEM work.

immunogold_labeling.reasoning: For the immunogold_labeling Process node, I included only labeling-protocol parameters that describe how antibodies and gold probes were applied to ultrathin sections. I excluded section geometry and grid properties because those belong to the upstream ultrathin_sections Entity, and I excluded the resulting labeled section properties, TEM capture settings, raw images, and computed localization outputs because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were supplied in this turn, so there were no existing field names to avoid. The fields focus on the operational details needed to reproduce the labeling step: primary antibody, probe conjugate, incubation conditions, washes, and a labeling success indicator.

md_schema.descr: Protein or epitope targeted by the primary antibody used during immunogold labeling of ultrathin sections, recorded at the labeling step; include the antigen name or tag recognized, e.g. GFP, HA, or the protein of interest name.
Host species in which the primary antibody was raised, recorded during immunogold labeling to document reagent identity; examples include rabbit, mouse, or goat.
Nominal diameter of the gold-conjugated probe particles used to visualize antibody binding during immunogold labeling, measured at the labeling step; report in nanometers, commonly 5-20 nm.
Temperature at which ultrathin sections were incubated with antibodies and gold-conjugated probes during immunogold labeling; typically 4-25 degrees Celsius depending on protocol.
Total incubation time for antibody and/or gold-probe exposure during the immunogold labeling step, measured in minutes; may range from tens of minutes to overnight depending on protocol.
Blocking reagent used before or during immunogold labeling to reduce nonspecific binding on ultrathin sections; examples include BSA, serum, or gelatin.
Number of wash steps performed after antibody or gold-probe incubation during immunogold labeling, recorded as an integer count to document stringency.
Outcome indicator for whether the immunogold labeling step produced usable section labeling prior to TEM imaging; use a controlled categorical assessment of the labeling result.

labeled_sections.reasoning: For the labeled_sections Entity node, I included only intrinsic properties of the immunogold-labeled sections that describe the state of the material after labeling and before TEM capture. I excluded the antibody, probe, incubation, and wash parameters because those belong to the upstream immunogold_labeling process, and I excluded microscope settings, raw file properties, and computed localization outputs because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no duplicate names to avoid. The selected fields capture the minimal entity-level metadata needed for downstream imaging and interpretation: labeling density, distribution pattern, background, and section usability.

md_schema.descr: Measured density of immunogold particles on the labeled section, recorded as an intrinsic property of the section after labeling and before TEM imaging; report as particles per square micrometer, typically used to quantify signal abundance.

Qualitative description of the observed distribution of gold particles across the labeled section before imaging, used to characterize whether labeling is localized or diffuse; examples include punctate, clustered, diffuse, or sparse.
Qualitative assessment of background or off-target immunogold signal on the labeled section prior to TEM capture, recorded as a section property; use standardized terms to indicate noise level.

Assessment of whether the immunogold-labeled section is suitable for TEM imaging after labeling, recorded before capture; use controlled values reflecting whether the material can be imaged and interpreted reliably.

Qualitative indication of whether immunogold signal appears enriched in specific organelles or compartments on the labeled section, recorded as an entity-level feature before imaging analysis; use broad categories only, not computed interpretation.

tem_capture.reasoning: For the tem_capture Capture node, I included only microscope session and instrument-configuration metadata: hardware identity, operating mode, and acquisition settings that were actively configured during TEM imaging. I excluded plant/sample properties, fixation/embedding/sectioning/labeling details, because those belong upstream, and I excluded file format, file size, and image dimensions because those belong to the downstream raw_tem_micrographs Signal node. I also excluded processed or biological interpretation fields because those belong to later Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied in this turn, so there were no prior field names to avoid. The selected fields focus on the minimum capture parameters needed to reproduce and interpret the TEM acquisition session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the transmission electron microscope used for image acquisition, recorded at the capture session; include the vendor name, e.g. JEOL, Thermo Fisher Scientific, or Hitachi.

Model designation of the transmission electron microscope used for acquisition, recorded at the capture session along with instrument identity; example formats include JEM-1400, Tecnai G2, or Talos L120C.

Instrument serial number of the transmission electron microscope used for the capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware; use the manufacturer-assigned identifier string if available.

Accelerating voltage used during TEM image acquisition, recorded as an actively configured microscope setting at the capture session; report in kilovolts, commonly within 60-300 kV depending on instrument and specimen.

Detector or imaging mode selected on the TEM during acquisition, recorded as an instrument configuration setting; examples include bright_field, dark_field, or camera-based readout modes used in the session.
Magnification setting used during TEM acquisition, recorded at the time each micrograph was captured; report as the nominal x-fold magnification value used on the microscope.

Effective pixel size at specimen level for the acquired TEM images, recorded as an acquisition calibration parameter for the session; report in nanometers per pixel, typically derived from magnification and camera calibration.

Camera exposure time used to acquire the TEM micrograph, recorded during the capture session as an actively controlled setting; report in milliseconds and use the value appropriate for each image acquisition.

Focus strategy or acquisition focus setting used during TEM capture, recorded to document how image sharpness was achieved; use controlled categories such as manual, automatic, or mixed if applicable.

raw_tem_micrographs.reasoning: For the raw_tem_micrographs Signal node, I included only raw data artefact properties: file identity, format, dimensions, size, and technical quality of the acquired micrographs. I excluded microscope settings and session configuration because those belong to the upstream tem_capture Capture node, and I excluded preprocessing, analysis, or localization fields because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no duplicate field names to avoid. The chosen fields are the minimum technical descriptors needed to store, validate, and reuse the raw TEM image files without interpreting their biological content.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw TEM micrograph file as stored immediately after acquisition, recorded at the signal level to identify the image artefact; example formats include image001.tif or sampleA_001.dm3.
Storage location or directory path where the raw TEM micrograph is saved, recorded for the signal artefact itself; use the repository path or filesystem path used in this workflow.
Technical file format of the raw TEM micrograph, recorded for the image artefact as acquired or exported from the microscope camera; examples include tiff, dm3, or mrc.
Size of the raw TEM micrograph file in bytes, measured for the stored signal artefact; useful for integrity checks and data transfer validation.
Horizontal dimension of the raw TEM micrograph in pixels, recorded for the signal file as stored after acquisition; report the actual pixel count of the image.
Vertical dimension of the raw TEM micrograph in pixels, recorded for the signal file as stored after acquisition; report the actual pixel count of the image.
Pixel intensity bit depth of the raw TEM micrograph, recorded as a technical property of the image file; common values include 8, 12, 16, or 32 bits per pixel.

Technical quality assessment of the raw TEM file immediately after acquisition, recorded as a signal-level flag indicating whether the image is usable without considering biological interpretation; use controlled categories for integrity or acquisition defects.

preprocess_tem_images.reasoning: For the preprocess_tem_images Process node, I included only processing parameters that describe how raw TEM micrographs were transformed into analysis-ready images. I excluded microscope acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream tem_capture Capture node, and I excluded file format, file size, and image dimensions because those belong to the downstream processed_tem_images Signal node. I also excluded biological interpretation and particle localization outputs because those belong to the later detect_gold_particles Process and localization_map Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no duplicates to avoid. The selected fields capture the minimum reproducible preprocessing details: software identity, calibration method, contrast/normalization operations, and a quality indicator for preprocessing outcome.

md_schema.descr: Name of the image analysis software used to preprocess raw TEM micrographs, recorded as a process agent property at the preprocessing step; examples include Fiji, ImageJ, or a custom pipeline.

Version of the preprocessing software used to calibrate, adjust contrast, and normalize raw TEM images, recorded at the processing step to ensure reproducibility; use the exact version string, e.g. 2.14.0.

Repository, package source, or codebase reference for the preprocessing software or pipeline used on the raw TEM micrographs, recorded at the processing step; include a URL, package name, or local repository identifier if available.

Method used to calibrate pixel scale or intensity in the raw TEM micrographs during preprocessing, recorded as part of the transformation step; examples include scale-bar calibration, camera calibration, or reference-grid calibration.

Contrast enhancement or adjustment method applied to raw TEM micrographs during preprocessing, recorded at the process step; examples include histogram stretching, gamma correction, or manual contrast tuning.

Intensity normalization method used to standardize raw TEM micrographs before particle localization analysis, recorded at the preprocessing step; examples include min_max, z_score, or percentile scaling.

Qualitative assessment of the preprocessing result for downstream particle localization, recorded after preprocessing and before signal handoff; use controlled values such as good, acceptable, or poor.

processed_tem_images.reasoning: I corrected the processed_tem_images schema by removing the colliding field name pixel_size_nm because it was already generated elsewhere in the DAG. To preserve the Signal node’s scope, I kept only output-file and output-quality descriptors that describe the processed image artefact itself. I did not reintroduce any upstream preprocessing methods or downstream analysis fields, and I avoided repeating any previously generated semantics while maintaining the minimum information needed for the processed signal.

md_schema.descr: Name of the processed TEM image file after calibration, contrast correction, and normalization, recorded for the signal artefact ready for downstream analysis; example formats include sampleA_preprocessed.tif.
Storage location or directory path of the processed TEM image file, recorded for the signal artefact as saved after preprocessing; use the repository or filesystem path used in the workflow.
Technical file format of the processed TEM image, recorded as a property of the image artefact after preprocessing; examples include tiff, png, or mrc.
Horizontal dimension of the processed TEM image in pixels, recorded for the output signal after preprocessing; report the actual pixel count preserved in the processed file.
Vertical dimension of the processed TEM image in pixels, recorded for the output signal after preprocessing; report the actual pixel count preserved in the processed file.

Whether intensity correction was applied to the processed TEM image during preprocessing, recorded as a signal property of the output image file; use true when calibration or normalization changed pixel intensities.

Technical quality flag for the processed TEM image after preprocessing, recorded for the output signal to indicate whether the file is suitable for downstream immunogold analysis without further correction; use controlled values only.

detect_gold_particles.reasoning: For the detect_gold_particles Process node, I included only computation-level parameters and outputs of the particle-detection analysis, not the upstream image-processing settings or downstream localization-map results. I also avoided the previously generated field pixel_size_nm as requested, and did not repeat any semantically equivalent capture/process settings. The fields focus on the analysis software, detection criteria, compartment mapping scheme, particle count, and a quality indicator describing whether the detection output is usable for downstream localization interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to detect immunogold particles in the processed TEM images, recorded at the detection process step; examples include ImageJ macro, custom Python pipeline, or commercial image analysis software.
Exact version string of the particle-detection software or pipeline used for immunogold analysis, recorded to make the analysis reproducible; example format 1.2.3 or commit hash if applicable.

Method used to threshold or classify gold particles during detection on processed TEM images, recorded as a process parameter; examples include fixed threshold, adaptive threshold, or model-based detection.
Minimum particle size in pixels accepted as an immunogold signal during detection, recorded at the analysis step to exclude noise; report as the lower bound used by the algorithm.

Maximum particle size in pixels accepted as an immunogold signal during detection, recorded at the analysis step to exclude merged or spurious objects; report as the upper bound used by the algorithm.

Rule set or ontology used to assign detected gold particles to cellular compartments during analysis, recorded at the detection step; examples include manual annotation, organelle ontology, or region-of-interest mapping.

Total number of immunogold particles detected and retained after filtering in the processed TEM image, recorded at the end of the detection process; report as an integer count for the analyzed field or image set.

Qualitative assessment of the particle-detection result for downstream localization analysis, recorded after detection is complete; use controlled values describing whether detections are reliable and complete.

localization_map.reasoning: For the localization_map Derivative node, I included only computed-result metadata: the analysis method that produced the map, key derived localization statistics, the compartment-level output structure, and a quality/confidence indicator for the final scientific result. I excluded sample preparation, TEM capture, raw/processed image properties, and particle-detection settings because those belong to upstream nodes. I also avoided repeating the previously generated pixel_size_nm field and any capture-scale terms. The selected fields are the minimum needed to interpret, reuse, and compare the derived protein-localization output across organelles and stress/photosynthesis-related compartments.

md_schema.descr: Name of the algorithm or analysis method used to compute the subcellular protein localization map from detected immunogold particles, recorded at the derivative step; examples include nearest-neighbor mapping, density estimation, or custom compartment-assignment pipeline.
Exact version string, release number, or commit identifier of the localization algorithm used to generate the protein localization map, recorded for reproducibility of the derivative result.

Ontology, naming convention, or manual annotation scheme used to label organelles and cellular compartments in the localization map, recorded as part of the derived output; examples include chloroplast, mitochondrion, cytosol, and nucleus.

List of cellular compartments represented in the final localization map, recorded as the output scope of the derivative; examples include chloroplast, thylakoid membrane, mitochondrion, cytosol, and nucleus.

Quantitative score summarizing the enrichment of tagged-protein signal in a target compartment relative to background in the final localization map, recorded as a derived metric; report on the scale used by the workflow, typically normalized or unitless.

Confidence assessment for the final protein localization map, recorded after computational derivation and reflecting how reliably the immunogold distribution supports the compartment assignments; use controlled categories for output certainty.

Indicator of whether the derived localization pattern is interpreted as relevant to photosynthetic efficiency or stress-response biology in the study context, recorded as a downstream interpretive flag for the final output; use a binary value.
